title: ACTION
blurb: Going, hurrying, pushing, striking and pulling.

radicals.name: STEP
radicals.origin: The left half of 行, a crossroads. It looks like the person radical 亻 with one more stroke on top, which is why teachers call it the double person.
ex: a long way to go on foot
stopping by the road until someone comes
radicals.watch: One stroke apart: 亻 (person) has one slanted stroke on top, 彳 has two. The hint has faded in its two commonest members, 很 (very) and 得 (to get).

radicals.name: RUN
radicals.origin: A person swinging their arms above a foot 止. In old Chinese 走 meant to run. Today it is the everyday word for to walk.
radicals.watch: Three radicals travel on foot. ⻊ (foot) stands on the left: 跑, 跳. 辶 (walk) wraps the bottom left in one smooth line: 进, 远. 走 wraps the same corner but keeps its whole shape.

radicals.name: STRENGTH
radicals.origin: A strong arm bent at the elbow. Others see a plough, the tool that took the most strength of all.
ex: it takes force to move something
radicals.watch: Look-alike: 刀 (knife) has nothing poking out at the top. In 力 the slanted stroke crosses through. 男 (man) has 力 underneath but is filed under field.

radicals.name: STRIKE
radicals.origin: A hand holding a stick, ready to tap or strike. It is named after 文 (writing), which it resembles, but it has a slanted stroke at the top left where 文 has a dot.
radicals.clue: doing something to something: hitting, changing, setting right
ex: driving something away with a stick
a child 子 and a teacher's stick. As a verb by itself it is read jiāo
radicals.watch: The hint is broad: an action with a result. Look-alike: 夂 has one stroke fewer and sits at the top or bottom of a character, as in 冬 (winter).

radicals.name: BOW
radicals.origin: An archer's bow with the string taken off, which is why it curls back on itself.
ex: drawing a bow opens it wide. Also the counting word for flat things
a bow and its string, pulled back
a bow that takes strength to draw
radicals.watch: Think of what a bow does: it bends, stretches and springs back. 弟 (younger brother) is filed here for its shape alone. 弹 is a pellet when read dàn, and to pluck or to bounce when read tán.
